meetings.headline: PACC will seek a November special town meeting warrant for more money as FY27 salaries run tight
meetings.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee (PACC) heard the station manager's monthly report on the Cablecast/Castis migration and video-on-demand rollout, reviewed and trimmed a draft list of FY27 goals (prioritizing a studio/storage space solution), and discussed a tight FY27 budget driven partly by a vacation payout. The committee voted to authorize preparing and submitting a warrant article for the November special town meeting to address the anticipated shortfall, and heard an update on the cable licensing/advisory committee's work toward eventual contract renegotiation with Comcast.

budget_items.what_was_said: The manager said FY26 books are not yet closed by the town, so the beginning balance shown is an estimate based on this month's figures and adjusted accordingly.

The manager said salaries will be a tight fit for the year because he opted to take his vacation time as a payout this year rather than spreading it over three years, which reduced the line item balance.

The manager raised whether PACC should submit a warrant for more money at the November special town meeting before a Thursday deadline, needing a dollar figure with high confidence of covering the year, possibly including capital items like the storage solution.
A member looked up a 16-foot storage pod rental as a possible equipment-storage solution and read out the monthly cost, noting it isn't in the current budget.
A member suggested buying and having delivered a shipping container as a one-time capital purchase instead of renting storage, out of capital funds.

A member asked if PACC is still paying rent of that amount; the manager said no, but there is a rent line item used for renting the FATV studio, which wasn't used in July but will be used in September and October.

Members discussed the legally capped franchise fee percentage on video services, recalling it was lower historically when more households had cable, and noted it cannot legally be raised above the current cap.

decisions.decision: The committee agreed to move the 'explore studio and storage space possibilities' goal up to top priority (goal A) in the FY27 goals list.

The manager agreed to consolidate the six draft goals into about four broader categories (local programming, government programming, process, storage space) per the town manager's request for fewer, more concentrated goals.

The committee agreed it could state now that a budget shortfall is anticipated and submit a warrant for the November special town meeting with details to be worked out later, consistent with past practice.
The committee agreed to leave 'studio space/master plan update' on the standing agenda even when there is nothing new to report, so it can be picked up if something comes up.
The committee set its next meeting date as October 5th.

meetings.headline: Failed town override cuts town concert funding and a town staff position, pushing website work onto PACC volunteers
meetings.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee handled routine business: minutes, a volunteer-applicant referral from the select board, the manager's monthly report, and a discussion clarifying that the failed town override (not the base FY2027 budget) is what cost the town its concerts and a town website/social-media staff position. The bulk of the meeting covered a consolidated policy/bylaw binder Steve compiled for review and eventual posting, an update on staffing the new cable advisory committee, and scheduling the July 6th meeting as an organizational meeting to fill two open PACC seats.

attendees.role: chair (conducted roll call, name not stated)

budget_items.what_was_said: The manager reported there are no town concerts because the override did not pass, so there is no funding for them.

A member clarified the override was meant to add extra funds on top of the base budget, not replace it; the base budget passed at town meeting regardless of the override's failure. Anyone counting on override money will not have it, though department heads may seek other adjustments.
It was noted that ordinary micro-adjustments happen within any budget (a role costs more or less, staff turnover) and these are called adjustments, distinct from the override question.
Line item transfers within the town budget are approved by the town manager; department heads can request them but need the town manager's sign-off, unlike in the past.

budget_items.topic: elimination of a town website/social media position
budget_items.what_was_said: Because the override failed, the town is eliminating a position handling website updates, social media and IT liaison work; PACC will informally take over doing the town website updates as a result.

January-through-March investment and interest was posted to the committee's account; the manager discovered the reported total interest actually combines two different bank sources (Main Street Bank and a second bank/entity) and will separate them going forward in Munis.
The committee had to buy a new eight-input ATEM switcher after the previous one burned out from hot-swapping, plus a new wireless transmitter and receiver after one failed.
The manager reported the purchase order for the Castus system was received; installation is not yet scheduled.
This report was not sent to the chair for the meeting because it was covered at the prior meeting.

decisions.decision: Moved the July 6th meeting from 3:00 p.m. to 6:00 p.m. because the town band concert that had driven the earlier time is not happening; meeting will be in the Wallace Room.
Agreed not to publish the town purchasing policy 'cheat sheet' in the committee's posted policy book because the full town version is for employees only and updates every six months.
Agreed to review the consolidated policy/bylaw sections one or two at a time each month going forward, starting with equipment use and drone policy.
Agreed that Steve (PACC) will take over doing the town website updates for the committee's own page, since the town position that did this is being eliminated.

Cable advisory committee membership set: Brian Leptonen (replacing Amanda, who resigned from the select board), Karen Menard, and Tom Bodkin, pending select board appointment; first meeting to be scheduled by contacting Cathy Herrick after June 16th.
Set the July 6th meeting, 6:00 p.m., as PACC's organizational meeting to fill two open committee seats and set the year's calendar.

meetings.headline: PACC began recruiting a citizen committee to renegotiate the town's Comcast cable license.
meetings.summary: This Public Access Cable Committee meeting was largely a manager's monthly report (staff retirement, town meeting recording, studio pack-up ahead of a building closure, and financial/budget figures) followed by discussion of outstanding policy documents and a review of an investment/trust account. The most substantive forward-looking item was launching the process to recruit residents for a separate committee to renegotiate the town's Comcast cable license ahead of its expiration, including engaging an attorney and planning a public survey. No major votes were taken beyond routine approval of amended minutes and adjournment, both without audible counts.

A committee member reviewed the principal placed in an investment account beginning around FY24, the amount presently in it, and an expected additional payment.

Each committee member will individually reach out to residents to recruit volunteers for the Comcast license renegotiation committee, aiming to have names by June.

meetings.headline: PACC approved its FY27 budget for FinCom, showing a shortfall to be covered from retained earnings
meetings.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee reviewed its manager's monthly report, walked through a detailed FY27 budget presentation destined for FinCom (salaries, new equipment, legal fees for upcoming Comcast contract negotiations, and Comcast franchise-fee revenue projections), and voted to approve the amended presentation and authorize the manager to present it. The committee also worked through a policy-book cleanup (an obsolete job title/policy to be formally removed), discussed early-stage talks about sharing studio space with FATV in Fitchburg, and voted to appoint two of its members to a newly approved town Cable Advisory Committee that will eventually handle Comcast franchise renewal.

budget_items.what_was_said: The manager said current-year salaries are on pace to exceed budget and will need a line-item transfer, and gave the FY27 salaries figure.
Videographer pay is budgeted to rise from FY26 to FY27.
Combined salaries and videographer costs rise from the FY26 to FY27 figure, an increase the manager characterized as double digits.
Both lines are unchanged from the prior year.
This line rises because the bulletin administrator's hourly rate was raised after it was found to be below minimum wage.
This line, used for video and peripheral equipment purchases via Amazon and B&H, is proposed to increase.
The large increase is to buy a new switcher and Castus program server plus installation, leaving a small remainder for emergencies.
A new legal fees line was added ahead of Comcast franchise negotiations, based on differing attorney fee estimates.
The insurance-driven indirect cost estimate was revised down after an initial higher estimate.
Revenue from Comcast fees was discussed amid concern about subscribers dropping Comcast; the quarterly basis used to project the year was revised downward after a lower recent quarterly payment.
Investment income was carried forward at the same level as FY26 because the finance department's interest postings are far behind.
The total PEG access revenue figure was corrected during discussion.
The manager gave a total expense figure and the resulting shortfall figure that would need to come from retained earnings, both to be updated after the Comcast revenue change.

The committee discussed asking the town to draw the shortfall from retained earnings via the warrant, noting timing problems because retained earnings for the year are not certified until after town meeting.
The budget presentation's funding-sources slide splits revenue between investment income and the Comcast franchise fee.

decisions.decision: The FY27 budget presentation, originally prepared for a tri-board meeting, will instead be given to FinCom on March 5.
Comcast revenue projection basis lowered to a more conservative quarterly figure rather than the higher one previously used, to avoid overstating expected revenue.
The manager will try to keep the FinCom presentation date but acknowledged FinCom may need to move it to give itself time to prepare questions.

The obsolete "videographer editor" job title/policy, which does not correspond to any actual town job title, will be brought back for a formal removal vote at the next meeting (policy changes require prior announcement).
A performance review needs to be added for the production technician position, currently missing from the review set; the manager will check with the town manager's office on the correct forms.
PACC will continue early-stage talks with FATV/Fitchburg about shared studio space, meeting again March 4, with many cost and legal details still unresolved.
PACC members will spread the word informally to find two more people for the newly approved Cable Advisory Committee, pending the Select Board's process.
No public announcement about cable advisory committee membership will be made until members are officially confirmed by the Select Board.

why_it_matters: The FY27 cable budget, funded mainly by Comcast subscriber fees rather than property taxes, still goes to FinCom for review as part of the town's overall budget process.

A shortfall covered from retained earnings means the committee is drawing down savings rather than raising fees this year, a choice that has a limit if adopted repeatedly.

minutes.headline: PACC to seek a meeting with the town manager after being shut out of two warrant changes
minutes.summary: The Public Access Cable Committee spent most of the meeting on its discovery that the town changed its annual and special town-meeting warrants without informing the committee, including an unexplained sum matching PACC's indirect/health-insurance costs and a dropped videographer salary increase. Rather than a formal vote, the committee decided to send one or two members to meet informally with the town manager about the warrant process and mutual expectations, and separately heard the manager's report showing a projected FY26 salaries shortfall, a possible move of the studio into the Ritter building, and unresolved questions about the Cable Advisory Committee's FY26 legal fees line.

what_happened.line: The committee found the annual town-meeting warrant had been changed before town meeting to add an unexplained sum, without anyone telling them.
A special-meeting warrant article meant to fix that also carried a small videographer pay increase, and the whole article was pulled before town meeting.
Rather than vote on the matter, the committee chose to send one or two members to meet informally with the town manager about the warrant process.
The station manager reported the salaries line is tracking toward a shortfall six months into FY26, with a firmer figure due in February.
A town committee is weighing moving the cable studio into the Ritter building's second floor.

why_it_matters: This is a dispute over whether a town committee's budget line can be changed on a warrant without notice to that committee -- a process question that could affect how any board's warrant article gets amended.
watch_next: A member will draft and circulate an email requesting a meeting with the town manager on the warrant process
FY27 budget update expected next month, ahead of a Tri-Board meeting
